Title: PKR congress opens amid electoral setbacks and reformist departures
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) heads into its national congress this weekend facing a problem that goes beyond recent electoral defeats: convincing Malaysians that it still has something to fight for.
The party is grappling with the departure of prominent reformist figures, internal dissent and poor results in Sabah, Johor and Negeri Sembilan, with another state election in Melaka looming.
For a party built around reform, equal treatment and institutional change, its time in government has brought another challenge: convincing voters those ideals remain relevant after nearly four years in power.
International Islamic University Malaysia political scientist Associate Professor Syaza Shukri said must  determine its political direction while rebuilding public trust.
“I think the biggest issue would be how to go forward. I think PKR is at a crossroads especially after losing people like Rafizi and now Izzah taking leave. They need to figure out what’s the trajectory,” she said.
“If it’s still a reform agenda then how to proceed with that now that trust is low. How to win back people’s support rather than just uniting around the leadership.”
A year of upheaval
PKR’s troubles intensified after last year’s party election, when then-deputy president Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli lost the post to Nurul Izzah Anwar, daughter of party president and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, by more than 5,900 votes.
Nurul Izzah secured 9,803 votes against Rafizi’s 3,866.
Rafizi subsequently resigned as economy minister, while Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad left his Cabinet post as natural resources and environmental sustainability minister after failing to retain his vice-presidential position.
A year later, both men resigned as MPs and left PKR. In May this year, they took over the Malaysian United Party and rebranded it as Bersama, positioning it as a new multiracial political platform ahead of the next general election.
Their departure was followed by signs of sympathy within PKR, with several lawmakers attending Bersama’s launch. The new party did not make an electoral breakthrough in Johor, but its presence added another complication for Pakatan Harapan, which was already facing Barisan Nasional despite the two coalitions being federal government partners.
(From left) Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad and Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli raise their hands together on stage during the official launch of the new political branding, Bersama, at the PJ Performing Arts Centre in Petaling Jaya on May 17, 2026. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
Three elections, three warnings
The electoral setbacks began in Sabah last November, where PKR won only one of the 12 seats it contested.
In Johor in July, PH won eight of the 56 state seats, down from 12 in 2022, with PKR securing only one through former education minister Maszlee Malik.
In Negeri Sembilan earlier this month, PH won 11 of the 36 seats and lost the state it had governed since 2018. PKR was reduced to two seats after losing four of its six incumbent constituencies.
The Negeri Sembilan result also highlighted the uneasy relationship between PH and BN, which contested separately while remaining federal government partners. BN subsequently worked with Perikatan Nasional in the state.
Syaza said the results should not automatically be read as PKR voters switching to rival parties, pointing instead to declining turnout, particularly among Chinese voters.
“Looking at recent elections, especially Johor and Negeri, it is not that PKR is losing support or support shifted to other parties. It’s just that a lot more people, especially Chinese voters, are choosing not to go out to vote,” she said.
“If that’s the case, the party needs to make a case to get them out, to mobilise them. And to do that the party needs to show it can fulfil the people’s expectations of PKR as the ruling party.”
Leadership and dissent
Questions over succession and dissent have also surfaced.
Nurul Izzah announced this month that she would step aside to pursue her studies. PKR subsequently granted her temporary leave, with vice-president Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail taking over her responsibilities.
Syaza said the episode highlighted PKR’s unresolved succession issue.
“It shows that the party has not settled the issue of succession and renewal and the next generation of leaders. It is still very Anwar-centric,” she said.
“So yes, now Amirudin is stepping up, but again it’s closing ranks behind Anwar’s faction with little dissent. That could both be good and bad. The party unites, but can it reinvigorate?”
Lee Chean Chung resigned from PKR’s central leadership council in June, saying the party was no longer what it was when he first joined.
Wong Chen then resigned as Subang MP earlier this week, ending his more than 10-year tenure in Parliament. He subsequently announced that he had left PKR and joined Bersama.
Wong, Lee and Ampang MP Rodziah Ismail have also raised concerns over their offices being blocked from accessing the MyKhas portal used to process constituency development allocations.
The dispute is politically sensitive for PKR, which has historically campaigned for equal allocations for elected representatives.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has defended the government’s position, saying constituency allocations are at the Prime Minister’s discretion and should ultimately reach constituents rather than be treated as an entitlement of individual MPs.
Syaza said the controversy nevertheless carried a political cost.
“PKR used to fight for equal allocation and now this happens. It unfortunately shows the grassroots that firstly PKR doesn’t tolerate dissent and secondly it affects the whole reformist facade and idealism it once carried,” she said.
Wong Chen then resigned as Subang MP earlier this week, ending his more than 10-year tenure in Parliament. He subsequently announced that he had left PKR and joined Bersama.
What does PKR stand for now?
For Syaza, the deeper problem is the transformation that comes with being in government.
“Being in government has changed the party. On one hand that is fine. Of course we understand opposition and government are two different forms, one with resources, one without, one with access, one demanding access,” she said.
“But the problem now is people don’t even understand what PKR stands for anymore. It’s okay if as a government they say their means of reform might be different but that language is barely even there.”
She said the congress should reopen political space within the party and redefine what PKR could offer Malaysians.
“PKR needs to reopen political space. How can it be a reform party if it stifles different opinions? It doesn’t make sense,” she said.
“Secondly, redefine what it wants to give Malaysians. They’ve been in power and supporters have not been very happy so what else can they do and offer, realistically?”
“It’s no longer just about forming a government. They’ve had the chance. What else?”
Look forward, not back
Akademi Nusantara senior fellow Prof Azmi Hassan said delegates should focus on the party’s future rather than dwell on its recent setbacks.
“With all the setbacks PKR is facing right now, I think the delegates want to see something in the future. Let’s move forward,” he said.
Azmi said PKR should use its position in government to develop strategies before the next election, while cautioning against attributing all of PH’s recent losses to PKR.
“True enough, Sabah, Johor, Negeri Sembilan, it is a setback. But again, they have to look at their contest as a Pakatan Harapan using one symbol,” he said.
“Yes, PKR lost a lot of seats in Sabah, in Johor, and also in Negeri Sembilan, but maybe it is because of the Pakatan Harapan structure. Maybe it is because of one of their allies, DAP for example, that’s bringing down PKR in this case. That needs to be looked at during the congress itself.”
Azmi also defended the government’s position on constituency allocations, saying the funds were intended for constituencies rather than individual MPs.
“I agree with this allocation against constituencies for those MPs that are not with PKR. And I think Datuk Seri Anwar is correct that the allocation is not for the MP, but for the constituencies itself,” he said.
Melaka test looms
The next test will come in Melaka.
Azmi said PKR needed to demonstrate that it had learnt from its electoral setbacks in Sabah, Johor and Negeri Sembilan before the state goes to the polls.
“Looking at the next general election, I think PKR needs to make a lot of adjustments. They did not do enough after Sabah, after Johor, and Negeri Sembilan, and Melaka is coming very soon,” he said.
“I think there is time to do some tweaking in terms of making a better presentation to the people in the Melaka state election.”
PKR has signalled that its congress will focus on reforms, economic development and strengthening the party, according to vice-president Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
PH wrested Melaka from Barisan Nasional in 2018, ending decades of BN rule, but the administration collapsed in 2020 following the Sheraton Move, after which BN took back the state government.
For PKR, the question now is whether it can retain its reformist identity while governing, make greater room for dissent and give voters a compelling reason to return to the ballot box.

Title: Fadhlina urges PKR members to focus on ideas instead of exploiting religion
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 14 — Political competition should be based on ideas and the ability to offer the best solutions to the people, rather than exploiting matters of faith for political gain, said Wanita PKR chief Fadhlina Sidek.
She said religious issues should be respected and should not be exploited for political gain, particularly during elections.
“Do not incite people over matters of faith or exploit religion arbitrarily. We also believe that the space available is an opportunity for us to broaden and compete in terms of ideas, concepts, and who can offer better solutions.
“It should not be about campaigning by disparaging one another,” she said when delivering her winding-up speech at the 2026 Wanita PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre in Ayer Keroh today.
Fadhlina also urged all PKR leaders and members to reconnect with the grassroots by strengthening ties with the people, including by understanding the community’s needs directly.
She said leaders at all levels of the party must be sensitive to the circumstances of the communities around them and take action to assist those in need.
“Look around your neighbours’ homes, as there may be many things that need our help. So, this is among the things that must also return to being our foundation with the people,” she said.
Fadhlina also reminded PKR members to remain loyal and steadfast in their commitment to the party’s struggle despite facing various trials and challenges.
She said the party’s strength must be built through hard work and the readiness of its machinery at all levels to ensure that the shared struggle with the people could continue.
“So, let’s continue our hard work, remain loyal, committed and confident in this struggle. Insya-Allah, I am very confident that we will do better,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Health minister warns contractors: Show progress or risk losing MOH projects
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) will not compromise on unreasonable delays in over 1,300 health facility development projects nationwide, and is prepared to terminate the contracts of contractors who fail to show convincing physical progress on-site.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said in a Facebook post today that such action is necessary to ensure planned projects are completed according to requirements so that the public can enjoy the benefits promptly, while also preventing the waste of public funds.
He noted that this matter was among those highlighted while chairing MOH’s Development Action Council (MTPK) Meeting No. 2 of 2026 this morning, which was also attended by representatives from the Public Works Department (JKR) and Finance Ministry.
Dzulkefly said that the MOH is also collaborating with the JKR, state governments, and utility companies to resolve issues affecting project implementation at the grassroots level.
In a related development, he said 10 major health facilities have been completed as of August, including the Northern Region Blood Centre in Kedah, the additional block of Tuanku Ampuan Najihah Hospital in Negeri Sembilan, and the Manjoi Klinik Kesihatan in Perak.
He also said that under the “Program Cakna Madani” initiative, 268 projects, or 37.75 per cent, have been completed, including improvements to the comfort of rural clinics, the expansion of haemodialysis centre capacities, and the replacement of obsolete equipment.
““Insya-Allah, I will ensure that every sen of the national health allocation is translated into a healthcare system that is more equitable, modern and comfortable for you all. Pray that our efforts are facilitated,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain ahead tonight for Selangor, Perak, Johor and four other states, MetMalaysia warns
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain, and strong winds expected to affect seven states until 9pm today.
In a statement, MetMalaysia said the affected states are Perak (Bagan Datuk, Muallim, Hilir Perak, and Batang Padang), Terengganu, Pahang, and Johor (Mersing).
A similar warning was also issued for Selangor (Sepang, Klang, Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor, and Kuala Langat), Negeri Sembilan (Rembau and Port Dickson), and Melaka (Alor Gajah and Melaka Tengah). — Bernama

Title: KTMB adds 124 ETS, EMU Plus services, nearly 39,000 seats for National Day, school holidays
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) is adding 124 services with 38,944 seats for its Electric Train Service (ETS) and Electric Multiple Unit (EMU) Plus services during the upcoming National Day and school holidays.
In a statement today, KTMB said 100 additional ETS services, offering 31,600 seats, would operate over 10 days from August 21 to 23, August 28 to 31, and September 4 to 6.
“These initiatives are part of KTMB’s efforts to increase capacity, expand travel options and meet rising passenger demand, particularly during the holiday season and National Day celebrations,” it said.
Additionally, 24 extra EMU Plus services, offering a total of 7,344 seats, will operate on selected dates from August 21 to September 6, including an extension of services to Bandar Tasik Selatan.
For the KTM Komuter’s northern sector, eight additional services on the Padang Besar-Butterworth-Padang Besar route will operate from August 27 to 31, bringing the total to 46 services daily on the route.
The statement said tickets for the additional services went on sale yesterday through KTMB’s official sales channels.
Meanwhile, KTMB also held various customer appreciation activities from August 10 to 14, including vouchers, KFC meals, free travel tickets and RM16 discounts to mark the ETS’ 16th anniversary.
Its group chief executive officer Datuk Azlan Shah Al Bakri said the strong performance of ETS over its 16 years of operation reflected customers’ high confidence in the reliability of the country’s rail transport system.
“Starting in 2010 with the route to Ipoh, the ETS service was expanded to Butterworth and Padang Besar in 2015 before further expanding southwards at the end of 2025,” he said.
He said the ETS, introduced on August 12, 2010, had now recorded 44.3 million passengers, with statistics for January to July this year showing a 56 per cent increase to 3.67 million passengers from 2.36 million in the same period last year.
The development reflected KTMB’s commitment to providing wider, more comfortable and competitive rail services while continuing to improve capacity, service reliability and the passenger experience, he added. — Bernama

Title: Free rides are over: LRT3 Shah Alam Line passengers start paying tomorrow
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 14 — After six weeks of enjoying free fares, passengers on the Light Rail Transit 3 (LRT3) Shah Alam Line will start to pay for their rides starting tomorrow (August 15).
Rapid KL in a statement announced that this includes the shuttle bus service as well as the Park N’ Ride facility.
“The implementation of this paid service marks another important phase in the operation of the Shah Alam Line after the six-week free travel period which was well received by the public.
“Rapid KL would like to express its gratitude to all users for their support, trust and willingness to choose public transport during the period,” the statement said.
Rapid KL also advised passengers to always prepare before starting their journey by ensuring their fare cards have at least RM5.
The public transport operator also informed that passengers can check the fare rates for the Shah Alam Line via the official MyRapid website.
“At the same time, concessionary fares via the MyRapid Concession Card are also available for eligible categories, including students, senior citizens and the disabled. Eligible passengers can use their respective concession cards to enjoy the set fare rates.
“Rapid KL welcomes the public to continue travelling with the Shah Alam Line and make public transport an option for easier, safer and smoother daily travel,” the statement said. — Bernama

Title: ‘Extraordinarily rash’: Prosecutor says police officer deliberately chased Ipoh teen before fatal crash
Article:
IPOH, Aug 14 — The High Court here was told today that the action of a senior police officer chasing a victim at high speed before crashing into him was described as a very dangerous act and showed “extraordinary rashness”.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Afzainizam Abdul Aziz in his rebuttal said that DSP Mohd Nazri Abdul Razak’s action of chasing Muhammad Zaharif Affendi Muhd Zamrie at close range was done with the knowledge that the act could result in death.
He said the accused was found not slowing down the Perodua Ativa he was driving even after passing a bump in the school area, but instead continued to follow closely before crashing into the victim at an intersection.
“The act by the accused was not only imminently dangerous, it is extraordinarily rash, it is crystal clear evidence of deliberate chase and tailgating by the accused against an unknown victim, a stranger, by following him closely after he left the school grounds.
“And when the accused got the opportunity, he hit him from the rear at the intersection, where the victim did not know that someone was actually behind him so close, chasing him,” he said.
Replying to doubts claimed by the defence, Afzainizam stressed that the absence of tyre tread marks on the victim’s body was not proof that the teenager had not been run over, instead citing the testimony of a pathologist that the thick clothing factor may have protected the marks although the possibility of the incident still exists.
Regarding the Event Data Recorder (EDR) data, Afzainizam said the speed and brake application information of the accused’s vehicle was obtained through special software by Perodua’s technical assistant who extracted the data without having to remove the hardware from the vehicle to maintain the integrity of the report analysis.
Judge Datuk Bhupindar Singh Gucharan Singh Preet set October 28 to decide whether Mohd Nazri, 46, should be called to defend himself on the charge of murdering Muhammad Zaharif Affendi, 17.
The prosecution was led by Afzainizam, assisted by Nasrul Hadi Abdul Ghani and Monisha Pandey, while the accused was represented by lawyers Datuk M. Athimulan, Datuk Mior Faridalathrash Wahid and Aiman Hakim Kamaruzzaman.
Mohd Nazri is charged with killing the teenager near Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Jati here, between 11.55am and 12.32pm, December 15, 2023.
The senior police officer is charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code which carries the death penalty or a minimum prison sentence of 30 to 40 years, and if not sentenced to death, he must be whipped not less than 12 strokes of the cane. — Bernama

Title: Chiba floods: Malaysians in Japan urged to stay alert, avoid unnecessary travel
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Malaysians in Japan are advised to avoid unnecessary travel and remain vigilant as unprecedented rainfall has triggered severe flooding and major transport disruptions across Chiba Prefecture and surrounding areas of the Kanto region.
The Malaysian Embassy in Tokyo said road and rail networks had been severely disrupted, leaving thousands of travellers stranded, including an estimated 7,000 people at Narita International Airport.
“Malaysians in Japan are advised to stay away from flooded or low-lying areas, exercise increased caution, remain vigilant and monitor local conditions closely, transport updates, evacuation notices and instructions issued by the Japanese authorities,” it said in a Facebook post on Friday.
At least eight people have died in the torrential rain that pounded eastern Japan, according to Kyodo News, while the Japan Meteorological Agency issued its highest Level 5 rain warning for more than one-third of the municipalities in Chiba Prefecture near Tokyo.
Evacuation orders were issued for more than 400,000 people at one point, while thousands of travellers were stranded overnight at Narita International Airport after flooding disrupted road and rail links, the report said.
The embassy also advised Malaysians to refer to the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) for the latest weather updates, warnings and advisories at www.jma.go.jp/jma/indexe.html.
It added that in the event of an emergency, Malaysians may contact the Embassy of Malaysia in Tokyo at +81-3-3476-3840 during office hours or the emergency hotline at +81-70-1471-9756 after office hours.
They may also contact the embassy via email at consular.tyo@kln.gov.my or mwtokyo@kln.gov.my. — Bernama

Title: Heading to Sepang? Expect road closures for Sukma cycling events from Sunday until Aug 19
Article:
SEPANG, Aug 14 — Several major roads in the Sepang district will be closed and traffic diverted in stages from this Sunday (August 16) until August 19 to make way for the road cycling event at the 2026 Selangor Malaysia Games (Sukma).
Sepang police chief ACP Norhizam Bahaman said the road closures would be implemented from 8.30am to 12.30pm throughout the period, involving the competition routes used by 142 participants.
He said a total of 96 locations would be monitored for traffic control duties throughout the event, divided into four zones.
“The four zones are Zone A, covering Jalan Pantai Sepang Putra-Sempadan Tumbuk; Zone B (Jalan Dengkil-Jenderam Hulu); Zone C (Jalan Jenderam-Salak); and Zone D (Jalan Salak Sepang-Sungai Pelek).
“All roads involved will be closed in stages from 8.30am to 12.30pm,” he said in a statement today.
He said that on August 16, 17 and 19, the routes involved included Persiaran Pantai Sepang Putra, Jalan Kampung Bagan Lalang, Jalan Bukit Bangkong-Tanjung Rhu and Jalan Tumbuk-Sempadan.
Meanwhile, he said the closure on August 18 would involve more routes, including Jalan Banting-Semenyih towards Dengkil, Pekan Dengkil, Jalan Jenderam Hilir, Jalan Jenderam-Salak, Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi, Jalan Pekan Salak-Lembah Paya, Jalan Sepang Lama and Jalan Sungai Pelek.
Norhizam said the Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division of the Sepang district police headquarters, with assistance from local authority enforcement officers and traffic personnel from the Selangor contingent police headquarters, would be stationed at road junctions and traffic lights, as well as conduct patrols and monitoring along the affected routes.
The public, particularly residents in the surrounding areas and road users, are advised to plan their journeys in advance and use alternative routes to avoid congestion.
Sukma Selangor 2026 is scheduled to take place from tomorrow (August 15) to August 24, while Para Sukma 2026 will be held from September 5 to 14. — Bernama

Title: Bentley owner wins RM900,000 payout after Kelana Jaya crash, Appeals Court rejects staged-accident claim
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 14 — The Court of Appeal here today upheld a High Court decision ordering an insurance company to pay RM900,000 in indemnity to a businessman for damages to his Bentley Continental in an accident in 2020.
A three-member bench comprising Justices Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing, Datuk Ismail Brahim and Datuk Leonard David Shim dismissed both MSIG Insurance (Malaysia) Bhd’s appeal and Inderpal Singh’s appeal, with RM50,000 in costs each.
MSIG Insurance had appealed against the High Court’s decision allowing Inderpal’s claim for indemnification under the insurance policy, while Inderpal appealed against the dismissal of his claim for negligence and consequential claims for RM253,000 for loss of use and RM990,000 for loss of enjoyment of the luxury car.
Delivering the unanimous decision, Justice Choo said the court found that the High Court judge had evaluated the evidence and made findings of fact that disclosed no error warranting the Court of Appeal’s interference.
He said although there was a version put forward by MSIG Insurance as to how the accident could have happened, that could not move this court to disturb the trial court’s finding.
Justice Choo said that the court was not convinced by the suggestion that the accident was staged to claim insurance.
“There was no evidence which was convincing that Inderpal Singh had staged the accident, other than the defendant’s (MSIG Insurance) suspicion that the accident could not have happened in a manner as proffered by Inderpal Singh,” he said, adding that occasionally, accidents could happen without a scientific and logical explanation.
On Inderpal’s cross-appeal, he said the court agreed with the High Court that Inderpal had failed to prove that MSIG Insurance was negligent in carrying out the investigation and processing his insurance claim.
Inderpal is the registered owner of the Bentley Continental which was insured with MSIG Insurance under a private car insurance policy providing comprehensive coverage valued at RM900,000 for one year beginning from February 8, 2019.
On January 22, 2020, Inderpal was returning home after visiting his sister in Kelana Jaya when his vehicle collided with a guardrail on the left side of the road after he attempted to avoid hitting a dog that had unexpectedly crossed his path.
He notified an MSIG insurance agent the following day, and the vehicle was subsequently towed to a workshop, which prepared an estimate report detailing repair costs amounting to RM1,053,491.07.
On June 4, 2021, MSIG Insurance issued a letter rejecting Inderpal’s claim, alleging that it was suspicious and inconsistent with the circumstances of the accident as described by Inderpal.
The insurer also alleged that Inderpal had used fraudulent means to obtain benefits from the insurance policy.
Inderpal filed a suit seeking indemnification under the insurance policy, alleging breach of contract and negligence by the insurance company in handling his claim.
On May 20 last year, the Kuala Lumpur High Court allowed Inderpal’s claim for indemnification under the insurance policy but dismissed his claims for negligence and consequential claims for loss of use and loss of enjoyment of the car.
Inderpal was represented by lawyers David Samuel and Mithurran Ravinthiran, while lawyer Samreet Singh Sagoo and Theebadarshini Retnakumar represented MSIG Insurance. — Bernama

Title: Zahid: Bagan Datuk has potential to become competitive, liveable town
Article:
IPOH, Aug 14 — Bagan Datuk has the potential to be developed as a livable, competitive and distinctive administrative town in a park, with good facilities and infrastructure, broader economic opportunities and a comfortable environment for the people.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who is also the Bagan Datuk Member of Parliament, said the parliamentary constituency had tremendous potential, and it was the responsibility of relevant stakeholders to ensure that every potential was translated into development that benefits the people.
“I started the day in Bagan Datuk by listening to a presentation on the study report for the Bagan Datuk special area plan (RKK) with the Teluk Intan Municipal Council, Bagan Datuk District and Land Office and the consultants.
“As a native of Bagan Datuk, I certainly want to see this district that we love continue to develop through well-planned development that takes into account the needs of the local community,” he said in a Facebook post.
“I have always believed that our Bagan Datuk has tremendous potential, and our task is to ensure that every potential is translated into development that ultimately benefits the people.
“Insya-Allah, we will continue to strive for the best for Bagan Datuk,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia to prioritise safety of Myanmar refugees before repatriation, says foreign minister
Article:
SEREMBAN, Aug 14 — Malaysia will prioritise the safety of Myanmar refugees before repatriating them to their home country to ensure their welfare and lives are protected.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said cooperation between the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and the Home Ministry (KDN) was important to verify the refugees’ status and assess the security situation they would face upon return.
“I have asked the Secretary-General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to liaise with the Myanmar government through its embassy so that they can be brought back gradually,” he told reporters after a Ziarah Kasih programme at Taman Pinggiran Senawang here today.
On media reports stating that the Myanmar government was prepared to repatriate 5,000 of its nationals in Malaysia by ship, he said Malaysia was ready to do it in stages, with priority given to those whose status had been verified.
“There is no need to wait until there are 5,000 people. The 1,000 already identified for repatriation can be sent back,” he said.
Mohamad said Asean also viewed the issue of Myanmar refugees seriously and that it needed to be addressed collectively by member states.
He added that the Five-Point Consensus (5PC) must remain the core of the Asean mechanism in addressing the crisis in Myanmar. — Bernama

Title: Education minister: Pupil protection policy clarifies roles, does not burden teachers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — The School Pupil Protection Policy is not intended to place sole responsibility for pupil safety on teachers, but to establish a clearer framework defining the roles of all parties in safeguarding pupils’ safety and well-being.
Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said the policy provided structured guidelines on the actions to be taken by various stakeholders when concerns arose over pupil safety and welfare.
“This policy creates a clearer framework regarding who should do what when concerns arise regarding the safety and well-being of a pupil. What we need from teachers is not to remain silent when there are concerns about a child’s safety.
“Upon receiving a complaint or having reasonable suspicion, report it immediately to the administrators. Teachers do not need to wait until they have complete evidence to make a report,” she said in a Facebook post today.
Fadhlina said the Ministry of Education (MOE) would intensify engagement sessions and briefings to address educators’ concerns and clarify their roles, adding that such sessions had already been held with the National Union of the Teaching Profession (NUTP), Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (SUHAKAM), United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) and several non-governmental organisations (NGOs).
She said pupil protection involved a broader ecosystem comprising the MOE, State Education Departments (JPN) and District Education Offices (PPD), as well as external agencies such as the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and Social Welfare Department (JKM).
She said once a report was lodged, the case would be coordinated and appropriate action determined based on its nature and severity, including referral to relevant authorities where necessary, to prevent pupils from suffering repeated trauma due to improper case handling.
“I understand that a single document will not answer every question. That is why briefings and engagements must continue until teachers truly understand their roles, know the limits of their responsibilities, and feel confident about the steps to take when confronted with an incident,” she said.
Fadhlina also assured that the MOE would not leave teachers to act alone in protecting pupils, including by providing legal assistance where necessary and appropriate, stressing that the policy was not aimed at finding fault or turning teachers into scapegoats. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak plans third cloud seeding operation amid prolonged hot, dry weather
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 14 — The Sarawak state government, in collaboration with the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), is planning to carry out a third series of cloud seeding operations (OPA) in the state soon.
State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) chairman Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas said the mitigation measure was aimed at addressing prolonged hot and dry weather conditions that could affect water supply sources and worsen haze in several areas.
“The main focus of OPA Series 3 will be on identified critical dam and water catchment areas, particularly those important for ensuring the continuity of water supply and maintaining dam levels.
“The implementation is subject to the availability of suitable clouds, atmospheric conditions and favourable meteorological factors,” he said in a statement today.
Uggah said the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) would continue conducting technical analysis and assessments to determine the suitable locations, timing and atmospheric conditions before the operation is carried out.
He said the current hot, dry and hazy conditions had increased the risk of open burning and reduced air quality in several districts.
“Prolonged hot and dry weather could affect air quality, water supply sources and increase the risk of forest, peatland and open area fires.
“Therefore, Sarawak JPBN and relevant agencies are continuously strengthening monitoring of weather developments, air pollution levels, hotspots, forest and peatland fires, as well as water supply status,” he added.
As of noon today, nine locations recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, with Serian recording the highest at 182, followed by Kuching (171), Samarahan (170), Sri Aman (162), Sarikei (158), Mukah (151), Bintulu (151), Tebedu (150) and Lundu (102). — Bernama

Title: Six-month traffic diversion begins today along Damansara-Shah Alam NKVE
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — A traffic diversion will be implemented along the Damansara-Shah Alam route at KM13.60 to KM14.35 in both directions of the New Klang Valley Expressway (NKVE) for six months, from today until February 9, 2027.
PLUS Malaysia Berhad, in a statement today, said the diversion is to facilitate the construction of a pedestrian bridge across the highway, as well as maintenance works by Pinnacle Homes AD Sdn Bhd.
In this regard, PLUS advised motorists to comply with all traffic signs and instructions from PLUS personnel to ensure smooth traffic flow and the safety of all parties.
PLUS also recommended that motorists plan their journeys and obtain the latest traffic information through the PLUS app, its official social media platforms, including X @plustrafik, and variable message signs at selected locations.
“If there is an emergency, highway users can contact PLUSLine at 1-800-88-0000 for assistance,” it said. — Bernama

Title: Flash floods hit parts of Puncak Alam after hour-long downpour (VIDEO)
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 14 — Flash floods have hit several areas in Puncak Alam following about an hour of heavy rain in the afternoon today, with about one foot of water recorded along Jalan Persiaran Puncak Alam 6.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations division asst director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said six firefighters from Bestari Jaya Fire and Rescue Station conducted flood risk assessment in the area at 3.45pm, and found that the road was inundated in a foot of water, adding that no evacuation of residents was conducted.
Meanwhile, social media was abuzz with users sharing the flash flood situation in Puncak Alam, with Threads user dayangd_na sharing a video of conditions in a residential area and stating that flooding started following heavy rain of about an hour.
“It’s never flooded, now with just one hour of heavy rain, it rises up. I’m nervous because I’m worried about my car outside. Are others in Puncak Alam ok?” they posted.
Fellow Threats user _xmmmmmmmm shared a photo of flooding along Jalan Medan Puncak Alam, stating that he had to do a U-turn after several roads in the area were flooded.
“Info on flooded roads in Puncak Alam, guys. I’ve had to U-turn, just now towards Puncak Alam in front of the Ninso warehouse, left and right the roads are closed,” they posted.
Another Threads user akhrim_abs_official shared a video showing a flooded car sales centre along Jalan Persiaran Puncak Alam. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Govt measures help Malaysia weather West Asia crisis, sustain growth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — The government’s proactive response to the West Asia crisis, including financing support for affected small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and targeted fuel subsidies, helped sustain household spending and business activity in the country.
This helped contribute to the economy’s strong growth momentum into the second quarter of this year (2Q 2026), said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
“Reforms under the Madani Economy framework, together with proactive government measures, have helped shield the rakyat from the full impact of global supply disruptions while supporting consumption and economic growth,” Anwar said in a statement issued by the Ministry of Finance today.
Anwar, who is also the finance minister, noted that while disruptions to the global supply chains have exerted upward pressure on prices worldwide, Malaysia’s inflation remained contained at 1.9 per cent in 2Q 2026.
“The Madani Government has also continued to provide support through Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah, Sumbangan Asas Rahmah and targeted subsidy mechanisms under Budi Madani to cushion vulnerable households from rising costs,” he added.
Anwar also emphasised that while Malaysia’s growth momentum remains resilient, the Madani Government remains mindful that the benefits of economic growth are not felt evenly across households and businesses.
“Malaysia is not immune to the effects of these global disruptions. While the headline economic indicators remain encouraging, we recognise that many Malaysians continue to face pressures from the cost of living, while some workers and businesses are navigating a more difficult operating environment,” the prime minister said.
The Madani Government, he said, will therefore continue to prioritise measures that protect household purchasing power, support affected workers and businesses, and ensure that continued economic growth translates into higher incomes, better employment opportunities and tangible improvements in the lives of the rakyat.
Continued geopolitical uncertainty, disruptions to global supply chains, higher input and food prices, and employment pressures in certain sectors remain key risks to household well-being and business activity.
Against a global supply shock that has disrupted the world’s economy, Malaysia continued to defy expectations for the third consecutive quarter, growing by 6.0 per cent in 2Q 2026 compared with 5.4 per cent in the preceding quarter.
Powered by resilient domestic demand and a robust external sector, the country’s GDP growth exceeded both the Department of Statistics Malaysia’s advanced estimate and Bloomberg’s median forecast of 5.8 per cent. This marked Malaysia’s strongest second-quarter showing outside the pandemic period since 2014.
The 2Q 2026 performance brought growth in the first half of 2026 (1H 2026) to 5.7 per cent, placing the economy on a firm footing relative to the government’s full-year growth forecast of 4.0 to 5.0 per cent. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar hails stronger Q2 expansion, says govt shielded households from global inflation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today welcomed Malaysia’s stronger than expected second quarter growth, saying the 6 per cent expansion underscored the government’s efforts to shield households from global inflationary pressures.
In a Facebook post, Anwar described the second quarter growth as the country’s strongest performance outside the pandemic period since 2014, despite global supply disruptions and conflict in West Asia.
“This strength was made possible by the Madani government’s efforts to ensure the people’s lives were not severely affected by global inflationary pressures,” he said.
He cited initiatives such as Budi Madani, Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA), alongside behind the scenes measures to stabilise prices and maintain supply.
Anwar acknowledged that more work remained to sustain growth and ensure its benefits were widely shared. “We must guarantee meaningful incomes, quality job opportunities and assistance for vulnerable groups,” he said.
He added that the government would remain committed to reforms aimed at strengthening the economy and uplifting the people. “Insya Allah, the Madani government will stay on the reform path to raise the dignity of the people and reinforce the foundations of our beloved nation’s economy,” he said.

Title: Lim Guan Eng rebukes Penang CM Chow, disputes claim DAP delegates endorsed Umno partnership
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 14 — Lim Guan Eng has clarified that Penang Pakatan Harapan’s (PH) decision to work with Umno in the state government was not discussed at last week’s Penang DAP delegates’ meeting.
Lim said the meeting, attended by current secretary general Loke Siew Fook, focused solely on whether DAP should remain in the federal government, and not on Umno’s role in Penang.
He stressed that neither he nor any delegate raised the matter, as the agenda was confined to debating the pros and cons of staying in Putrajaya.
“However Chow should not presume that all Penang delegates endorsed his decision merely because no one raised it at Wednesday’s meeting when the Penang DAP delegates were focused on whether to stay or leave the Federal government in Putrajaya,” Lim said.
He criticised Penang PH chairman Chow Kon Yeow for commenting publicly on internal party discussions, saying only the secretary general had the prerogative to do so.
Lim added that Chow was entitled to continue working with Umno despite the party’s role in defeating Loke in Negeri Sembilan’s Chennah seat, but cautioned against assuming Penang delegates had endorsed the decision.
Lim’s remarks came a day after Chow said Penang PH was sticking with its decision to continue working with Barisan Nasional (BN), including Umno, despite Lim’s criticism.
Chow told reporters yesterday that the decision remained Penang PH’s position and was not challenged during the state DAP engagement session, adding that “no one questioned it”.

Title: Hop on, KK: BAS.MY pink buses expand eight routes, easing commutes across the city
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 14 — After four months of operation on its initial two routes, Kota Kinabalu’s new fixed-schedule BAS.MY “pink bus” service is now running across all eight routes, giving commuters more options for getting around the city and surrounding areas.
The full rollout of routes S01 to S08 began last Tuesday, completing the phased introduction of the service that started on April 1 with routes S01 and S05.
The first two routes have already recorded strong demand, with 194,265 passengers using the service between April 1 and August 10.
The figure is expected to increase with the addition of the six remaining routes — S02, S03, S04, S06, S07 and S08.
The expanded network is intended to make public transport a more practical option for daily travel, particularly for residents who do not own cars or motorcycles.
Buses now operate from 5.30am to 11pm daily, with services running at intervals of between 15 and 30 minutes.
A total of 48 new buses has been deployed to connect the main hubs at KK Sentral and Menggatal with the eight routes.
The service also offers free concession cards to students, senior citizens and persons with disabilities (OKU), with 960 people registered so far.
For commuters who depend on public transport, the concession scheme could help reduce the cost of daily travel, while the expanded network provides greater connectivity between residential areas and key destinations.
The buses are also equipped with real-time GPS monitoring, allowing their movements to be tracked, as well as cashless payment and e-ticketing systems.
Safety and accessibility features include closed-circuit television cameras and designs aimed at making the buses more accessible to senior citizens and persons with disabilities.
The full operation of BAS.MY Kota Kinabalu is part of the Federal Government’s Stage Bus Service Transformation (SBST) programme implemented through the Transport Ministry.
The programme involves an allocation of RM17.6 million a year, or RM88 million over five years.
Earlier this year, civil society group Sabah Entitlement and Equity Now (SEEN) and Api-Api assemblyman Loi Kok Liang raised questions about the fleet procurement of the buses.
The Sabah Commercial Vehicle Licensing Board (LPKP) subsequently defended the process, saying operator Jaguh Bayu Sdn Bhd was selected through the government’s ePerolehan system following technical and financial evaluations. LPKP also said the use of smaller buses was intended to suit Kota Kinabalu’s narrower roads and existing bus stops.
There were also concerns during the early rollout that awareness of BAS.MY remained low, with Kota Kinabalu MP Chan Foong Hin previously urging wider publicity to familiarise residents with the new service.

Title: Two women in dock for allegedly duping retiree in Perak out of RM120,000 over fake tax arrears
Article:
IPOH, Aug 14 — Two women were charged in the Magistrate’s Court here today with three counts of cheating a male retiree of about RM120,000 by falsely claiming they could help him settle his tax arrears.
Noorfarah Surina Ahmad, 42, and Nurfalah Noordin, 33, pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out before Magistrate S. Punitha.
The two women allegedly cheated Koay Kuang Hew, 60, by offering to help him settle his tax arrears, which actually did not exist, thereby dishonestly inducing Koay to give them the money, made in three transactions on April 10 and 14 and June 4 this year.
The offences were allegedly committed at Wisma Hasil, Jalan Tambun, in the Kinta district.
They were charged under Section 420 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same Code, which carries a maximum prison sentence of 10 years, a fine and whipping upon conviction.
Magistrate Punitha set bail at RM4,500 with one surety for each accused and set Sept 24 for mention.
Both accused were also ordered to report to the nearest police station once a month pending disposal of the case.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Zarris Sofea Zainudin appeared for the prosecution, while lawyers Izzat Fakhri Halimi and Intan Shafini Mior Shahrin represented Noorfarah Surina and Nurfalah, respectively. — Bernama

Title: From FOMO to future jobs: PKR Youth motions put Gen Z outreach in focus
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 14 — Youth issues took centre stage at the 2026 National Congress of Angkatan Muda Keadilan (AMK) today, with motions focusing on stronger engagement with Generation Z (Gen Z), jobs of the future, mental health and social wellbeing.
Three delegates from Perak, Terengganu and Sarawak called on PKR to refine its approach to better reflect the realities and needs of young Malaysians.
Syahnaz Putera Mohd Yaacob, who is Perak AMK Information chief, said PKR faced challenges in winning support from younger voters, particularly Gen Z.
He said the party needs a bolder and more creative approach to engage Gen Z, particularly through digital platforms, while helping them develop their talents and gain access to government opportunities and funding.
“It is a bitter reality we have to accept. Gen Z cast their votes simply because of FOMO, the fear of missing out. When their friends voted and flexed their inked fingers, so they vote too,” he said while tabling the motion.
Syahnaz also suggested helping young people register clubs and associations, giving them formal entities through which they could apply for funding and develop their talents.
Meanwhile, Terengganu AMK chief Md Asyraf Zulfadhly Md Zainudin tabled a motion on future jobs and the gig economy, aimed at expanding income opportunities for young people.
He proposed four measures, namely recognising the gig economy as an employment sector with comprehensive social protection; providing gig workers with pathways to upgrade their skills; expanding upskilling and reskilling programmes; and strengthening links between universities, Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institutions, and industry.
Separately, Christopher Jemat Amie, who is Sarawak AMK secretary, highlighted mental health and social wellbeing as key areas that should receive sustained attention under the reform agenda.
He urged the PKR leadership to make mental health and social wellbeing a continuing priority rather than an issue addressed only after tragedies.
“Make mental health and social wellbeing part of the reform agenda. It should not be seasonal or addressed only when tragedy strikes, but pursued continuously,” he said.
“We do not only want to build an advanced nation. We want to build a nation whose people progress as well,” he said. — Bernama

Title: ‘Datuk Seri’ businessman claims trial to RM37.1m company funds breach of trust at Bukit Tunku bank
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — A businessman with a “Datuk Seri” title pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court today to a charge of criminal breach of trust (CBT) involving RM37.1 million in company funds, allegedly committed four years ago.
Datuk Seri Zul Azmi Abu Hussin, 51, a director of Xspec Resources Sdn Bhd, was accused of misappropriating RM37,099,999.67 in company funds at a bank in Taman Tunku, Bukit Tunku here on Feb 15, 2022.
The charge was brought under Section 409 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years’ imprisonment, caning and a fine, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Siti Suriatey Mohamed Yusoff applied for bail of RM500,000 with one surety, along with an additional condition that the accused surrender his passport to the court until the case is concluded.
Zul Azmi’s lawyer Edly Mohammad Firdaus, however, applied for bail at RM50,000, citing that his client supports a wife, five children and elderly parents, and suffers from hypertension.
“My client was called in to give a statement today before being charged. He has fully cooperated with the investigation. Bail is not a form of early punishment, but to ensure the accused’s presence in court,” he submitted.
Judge Mohd Kafli Che Ali set bail at RM100,000 with one surety, along with the additional conditions sought by the prosecution, and fixed Oct 5 for case mention. — Bernama

Title: Illegal e-waste gets one-way ticket home as Malaysia targets 1,259 containers
Article:
PORT KLANG, Aug 14 — The Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) aims to return all 1,259 containers of illegal electronic waste (e-waste) to their countries of origin by year-end.
AKPS Port Klang commander Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal said the operation is being conducted in three phases of integrated enforcement, involving about 8,000 metric tonnes of seized e-waste over the past two years in collaboration with the Royal Malaysian Customs Department and Port Klang Authority.
“To date, we have shipped out 255 containers. We are now in the second phase, targeting the return of 533 containers of illegal e-waste.
“The third and final phase will begin on Oct 1, targeting the remaining 578 containers. The overall target of 1,259 containers is subject to any containers still under investigation,” he told reporters at the North Port Customs building here today.
Nik Ezanee said inspections have found no attempts to re-import the banned materials, though some containers have been detected returning with other commercial goods based on authority checklist reviews.
He said scanning machines at Port Klang remain highly efficient in detecting illegal shipments, but human weaknesses in their operation still pose challenges.
He acknowledged that there are occasional gaps, but said the agency continuously trains scanning officers to perform their duties well, and AKPS never stops improving its services.
On a related note, Nik Ezanee said the large-scale operation to return illegal e-waste reinforces the government’s commitment to ensuring Malaysian ports are not used as transit points or dumping grounds for toxic waste.
He said AKPS and other enforcement agencies remain committed to tightening risk profiling and taking stern legal action against any party attempting to violate laws and international conventions. — Bernama

Title: Three fight for one spot as vocational college applications surge past 67,000
Article:
TAIPING, Aug 14 — Applications for admission to Ministry of Education (MOE) Vocational Colleges (KV) have reached 67,045 nationwide as of today, against a capacity of 19,567 places.
Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh said the figure was expected to exceed 68,000 when applications close at midnight tonight.
He said this reflected strong interest in skills-based education, which was also reflected in the nearly 100 per cent employability rate recorded among KV graduates.
“The increase in applications proves the success of efforts by the Madani Government and the MOE to strengthen the TVET sector and subsequently boost graduate employability,” he told reporters after the signing ceremony for a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Toyo Tyre Malaysia Sdn Bhd and Universiti Malaysia Perlis (UniMAP) here today.
Wong said the employability rate of KV graduates reached 99.95 per cent in 2023, while rates of between 98 and 99 per cent had been consistently recorded in recent years.
He said close collaboration between the MOE and industry players ensured that the fields offered and skills acquired by KV students met job market requirements.
“This exceptionally high employability rate shows that collaboration with industry is vital to ensure the fields offered and skills acquired meet job market requirements,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Eighteen lives lost daily is tough to stomach, but Works Ministry data is finally pointing to the fix
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 14 — The use of the Road Accident Management System (RAMS) has enabled the Ministry of Works (KKR) to identify 99 locations where fatal accidents frequently occur or ‘blackspots’ on federal roads nationwide.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said RAMS, developed by KKR under the MYJalan initiative, plays a role in systematically managing, analysing and displaying road accident data, including identifying locations where accidents frequently occur.
“The average of almost 18 lives lost every day due to road accidents in Malaysia is a very worrying figure,” he told reporters after officiating the closing ceremony of the RAMS Expansion Course and Road Accident Data Reporting here, today.
He said through the integration of accident data from the Integrated Police Reporting System (IPRS) under the supervision of the police, RAMS enables the planning and implementation of road safety interventions to be made more accurately and quickly.
“Accurate and quality data is an important basis in planning safer, more efficient and sustainable road infrastructure,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Bukit Mertajam Hospital makes global green list, ranks among world’s top 250
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM, Aug 14 — Bukit Mertajam Hospital (HBM) here has made history by being ranked among the 250 greenest hospitals in the world in the World’s Greenest Hospitals 2026 ranking by Newsweek and Statista.
The Ministry of Health (MOH) said the achievement recognised HBM’s commitment to implementing climate-friendly healthcare practices and environmental sustainability.
“More importantly, HBM was selected, beating thousands of other hospitals from 36 countries in this inaugural edition, which recognises healthcare institutions worldwide for their outstanding commitment to climate-friendly healthcare and environmental sustainability.
“This proves that the sustainable healthcare agenda at MOH is not merely a campaign, but a real and continuous effort to build hospitals that are greener, more efficient and future-ready,” MOH said in a post on its Facebook page today.
MOH also congratulated the entire HBM staff and the MOH Engineering Services Division, which were instrumental in the hospital’s sustainability achievement. — Bernama

Title: Bukit Aman say they know how Malaysia Airlines pilot cleared KLIA checks after three-day interrogation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Police are pursuing members of a drug syndicate in Malaysia after a Malaysia Airlines pilot was arrested in Jakarta late last month with more than 26 kilogrammes of drugs in his luggage.
According to
Berita Harian
(BH), Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the operation followed intelligence obtained after investigators interrogated the pilot over two days.
He said the questioning enabled police to gather information on syndicate networks in Malaysia and abroad, as well as the individuals involved. Hussein added that further details could not yet be disclosed publicly.
He said NCID had received strong cooperation from the Indonesian National Police (POLRI) during the investigation. The questioning, initially scheduled for August 12 and 13, was extended until August 14, and the pilot was reported to have given full cooperation.
Hussein said the investigation also allowed NCID to share key intelligence on international drug syndicates with relevant agencies.
“The team also learned how the suspect bypassed checks at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) and about the syndicate’s financial flows at home and abroad,” he told BH.
The case involves a 39-year-old Malaysia Airlines pilot who was arrested shortly after arriving at Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport from Kuala Lumpur on July 28.
Indonesian authorities said more than 26kg of ecstasy tablets and a packet of methamphetamine were found in a suitcase the pilot collected after customs officers flagged it during an X-ray inspection.

Title: Married couple plead guilty to causing death of three-month-old baby under their care in Johor
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 14 — A husband and wife were charged in the Sessions Court here today with causing the death of a three-month-old baby boy who was under their care in Masai last month.
The accused, Mohd Iqbal Hassan, 36, and his wife, Norsiayana Abd Samad, 34, pleaded guilty after the charge was read to them before Judge Datuk Che Wan Zaidi Che Wan Ibrahim.
According to the charge sheet, the couple, as persons having custody of Muhammad Saif Mohamad Sidiq, exposed the baby in a manner likely to cause him physical injury, resulting in his death.
The offence was allegedly committed at 1.03pm at a house in Jalan Cendana 21, Taman Rinting, Masai, on July 29.
They were charged under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001, which provides for imprisonment of up to 20 years, a fine of up to RM50,000, or both upon conviction.
The charge was read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code, which deals with joint liability.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Shamira Mohd Luthfi Ismail prosecuted, while the couple were represented by K. Bharathi of the National Legal Aid Foundation (YBGK).
During the proceedings, Bharathi requested minimum bail for his clients.
He said Mohd Iqbal, a factory worker, earns RM3,000 a month, while Norsiayana earns RM2,000 as a nanny, and that the couple have a four-year-old child.
The court granted bail of RM7,000 to each accused and ordered them to report to the nearest police station once a month and surrender their passports to the court.
They were also prohibited from interfering with prosecution witnesses.
The court set September 17 for the presentation of the facts of the case and sentencing.

Title: ECRL Kota Bharu–Gombak service targets December 2026 launch, a month ahead of schedule
Article:
GOMBAK, Aug 14 — The East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) Phase 1 service from Kota Bharu to Gombak is targeted to commence operations as early as December, earlier than the original schedule in January 2027.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the target depends on the smoothness of the ongoing testing and commissioning processes, including the System Integration Testing (SIT) and Fault-Free Run (FFR), without any compromise on safety aspects.
He said Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) and the main contractor China Communications Construction Company Ltd (CCCC) need to work to expedite the process so that the service from Kelantan to Selangor can commence by the end of this year.
“We are trying to see how the Land Public Transport Agency (APAD) can help facilitate matters related to the testing and certification processes to expedite this project without compromising safety.
“Usually, it takes two to three months, so we want to see how we can shorten that time,” he said at a press conference after the launch of the Comprehensive Inspection Train (CIT) and the Introduction of the Main ECRL Station Design Concept, as well as the Start of the SIT and FFR ECRL Project at the Gombak Integrated Terminal Station here today.
Loke said the effort to accelerate the operation was made based on the assessment that various tests on the train had been conducted before it was sent to Malaysia, including tests at the factory in China.
According to him, the SIT ECRL starting this month will test the integration of various systems including electrical and signalling systems before the FFR is implemented in September.
He said the first train set and E-Loco each need to undergo FFR over a distance of 8,000 kilometres under the supervision of APAD to ensure that operational safety and reliability meet the established standards and legal requirements.
“FFR is one of the important processes before commercial operations because the train will move on the track under real conditions, but without carrying passengers,” he said.
Loke said that all previous tests must be completed and approved before the FFR is implemented, therefore the effort to expedite the period does not mean that any safety processes will be overlooked.
“We are more afraid than you. I am more afraid than you if there is a risk. Of course, we take all considerations into account,” he said.
Meanwhile, he also said the ECRL project has now recorded an overall progress of 95.08 per cent as of July for Phase 1, which connects Kota Bharu and Gombak.
He added that Phase 2, which connects Gombak to Port Klang, is expected to be completed by December 2027, with operations scheduled to begin in January 2028.
Also present at the event were the Chief Secretary to the Government and MRL chairman Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Haji Habibollah, the Chinese Ambassador to Malaysia Ouyang Yujing, and Ministry of Transport secretary-general Datuk Seri M. Jana Santhiran, MRL chief executive officer Datuk Seri Darwis Abdul Razak and CCCC president Zhang Bingnan. — Bernama
